questions.question: Why RC coupling is preferred in multi stage amplifier design? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Why RC coupling is preferred in multistage amplifier design?
  • RC coupling is widely used because it offers excellent frequency response, a simple
  • construction, low cost, and a compact size. It passes AC signals while blocking DC,
  • ensuring each stage is properly biased without affecting the next. It also maintains
  • good signal fidelity and has minimal distortion.
  • Marks distribution: Concept (2), Advantages (3) = 5 marks

  • biased. The transistor conducts heavily, and collector current is maximum and
  • independent of base current. Collector-emitter voltage (Vce) drops to a low value
  • (~0.2V). The transistor behaves like a closed switch.
  • Marks distribution: Definition (2), Junction condition (1), Characteristics (2) = 5

questions.question: Why is the open-loop op-amp gain considered impractically high for analog signal amplification? / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is the open-loop op-amp gain considered impractically high for analog
  • signal amplification?
  • The open-loop voltage gain of an op-amp (typically 10⁵–10⁶) is so high that even a
  • small input differential voltage drives the output to saturation (±V_sat). Hence, direct
  • analog amplification is not practical. To ensure linear operation and controlled gain,
  • feedback (usually negative) is introduced.
  • Marks distribution: Concept (2), Reason (2), Solution (1) = 5 marks

questions.question: What is the operating point of a BJT? Explain.Why is it so important? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the operating point of a BJT? Explain why it is important.
  • The operating point (Q-point) represents the steady-state values of collector current
  • (Ic) and collector-emitter voltage (Vce) when no input signal is applied. It defines the
  • transistor’s DC bias condition.
  • A proper Q-point ensures the transistor operates in the active region for faithful
  • amplification. If not chosen properly, the output may distort due to cut-off or
  • saturation. Graphical method using the DC load line can be used to locate the Q-
  • point.
  • Marks distribution: Definition (2), Importance (3), Explanation with load line (3),
  • Diagram & clarity (2) = 10 marks

questions.question: Compare the transition from SSI to VLSI in integrated Circuit? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the transition from SSI to VLSI in Integrated Circuits.
  • • SSI (Small Scale Integration): up to 100 components per chip; used in basic
  • logic gates.
  • • MSI (Medium Scale Integration): 100–1,000 components; used in counters and
  • registers.
  • • LSI (Large Scale Integration): 1,000–10,000 components; used in simple
  • processors.
  • • VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration): >10,000 components; used in
  • microprocessors, memory chips.
  • The evolution from SSI to VLSI led to smaller size, lower power consumption,
  • higher speed, and improved reliability. Moore’s Law describes the exponential
  • growth of integration levels.
  • Marks distribution: Explanation of stages (6), Comparison & examples (2),
  • Evolution impact (2) = 10 marks
